title: Engineering Design
seo_title: Grade 5 Engineering Design Worksheets: Criteria, Constraints, Fair Tests and Prototypes
standard_text: Define a simple design problem reflecting a need or a want that includes specified criteria for success and constraints on materials, time, or cost. Generate and compare multiple possible solutions to a problem based on how well each is likely to meet the criteria and constraints of the problem. Plan and carry out fair tests in which variables are controlled and failure points are considered to identify aspects of a model or prototype that can be improved.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 science worksheets on engineering design (NGSS 3-5-ETS1): criteria and constraints, comparing solutions in tables, fair tests, failure points and improving prototypes. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: A good design meets every criterion within its constraints.
key_sub: Criteria are goals; constraints are limits on materials, time or cost. Test fairly, find failure points and improve.
body_html:
How to think about it

Engineers solve problems step by step:

  1. Define the problem. List the criteria (what success looks like) and the constraints (limits on materials, time or cost).
  2. Think of several solutions and compare how well each one meets the criteria and constraints.
  3. Build a prototype and test it fairly. Change one variable at a time, repeat the trials, and look for failure points.
  4. Improve the design and test again.

If a bridge must hold at least 20 pennies and cost no more than $5, only Design A works. Design B holds the most but costs too much.

Example

“The boat must hold 50 marbles” and “use only one sheet of foil.” Which is the criterion?

The goal is holding 50 marbles.

One sheet of foil is a limit.

Answer: holding 50 marbles

Example

Trials: 18, 22 and 20 pennies. What is the mean?

18 + 22 + 20 = 60

60 ÷ 3 = 20

Answer: 20 pennies

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up criteria (goals) and constraints (limits).
  • Picking the design that is best at one thing even though it breaks a constraint.
  • Changing more than one variable in a test.
  • Trusting a single trial instead of repeating the test.

faq.q: What is the difference between criteria and constraints?
faq.a: Criteria are what the design must do to succeed, like holding 20 pennies. Constraints are limits, like using only 5 sheets of paper or spending no more than $5.
A test where only one variable changes and everything else stays the same, repeated several times.
A part of a design that breaks or does not work during testing. It shows what to improve.

faq.q: What are the steps of the engineering design process?
faq.a: Define the problem, think of and compare solutions, build and test a prototype, then improve it and test again.

items.q: A class is designing a container that keeps an egg from breaking when dropped. Which statement is a constraint (a limit)?
c: The egg must be easy to take out.
The container must weigh less than 200 g.
It must span the whole 30 cm gap.
The egg must not crack when dropped from 3 meters.
items.e: Constraints limit the materials, time or cost. The others are criteria for success.

items.q: Why do engineers think of several possible solutions?

because the first idea is always wrong

items.e: Comparing options leads to better designs.
